q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a pair of jeans?
title: Denim jeans carbon footprint per pair
short: Multiply the denim fabric per pair, including cutting waste, by your mill's per-metre or per-kg factor. Add trims, sewing electricity, washing and finishing fuel and chemicals, and packing. Divide by pairs passed. Fabric is usually most of the total, then washing.

ul: Count fabric issued per pair from your marker plan, including the cutting waste.
Ask the denim mill for a figure per metre or per kg; cotton growing, spinning, dyeing and weaving are all in it.
Stretch denim includes elastane, which is higher per kg than cotton.
Washing: boiler steam for hot washes, enzymes, stones, bleach and dryers. Laser and ozone finishing cut water and chemicals.
Rivets, buttons, zips, labels and the poly bag.

p: Divide by pairs that pass inspection. Give heavy and light washes separate figures if your wash recipes differ.

example.title: Worked example: jeans unit per pair (one month)
lines: Wash boiler PNG: 15,000 SCM x 2.05 = 30,750 kg CO2
Plant total: 73,350 / 100,000 = 0.734 kg CO2 per pair
Add denim fabric, trims and chemicals for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
